This document produced after the 1st revision by a new doc number
 DsR-001-r1 according to the approved MPIS coding system, will be used instead of document
 # PC-SS-001-r0

This document lists the 
 testing procedures P1 for L8b distance relay, which must be 
 performed on an annually bases Y1 as indicated in the title block.
Safety Precautions

items: Line Isolation and work permit required.
Make sure CT secondary circuits are shorted.
Voltage Supply to the relay may be alive even after the line is isolated.

Isolate DC supply to relay. When doing any adjustments or maintenance on
 the L8b relay itself
Ensure all CT path elements are secure after any test disturbance.
ABB Relay Test Set Type QZW 415 Voltmeter,
Ammeter 5 amp, Phase rotation meter,

Small slot screwdriver, Test leads, 
 timer, and
5 amp. clip-on ammeter (optional)

sections.text: Work to be Carried Out

Review technical reference material: Manufacturer's manual and the P5 Course-L8b 
available from Technical Services.
Obtain copy of relay's setting specification from field maintenance file
Obtain outage for line protected by this relay.
Check that the bus and line disconnect switches are opened and tagged.
Block protection signals to: Breaker trip coils and transfer trip scheme(s).

Go to the switchgear and inspect the CT's, the VT miniature circuit breakers 
(MCB's), and all cabling supplying the relay:

Check that the cables are in good condition and that all wire connections 
are tight and clean.

Look at the EEC panel nameplate and check that this EEC system designation 
nameplate agrees with the line that has been taken out of service for 
maintenance.

Perform one of the following ammeter checks to
 verify there is no current flowing through this relay and that the testing
 will occur on the correct relay: 
(i) Using a clip-on ammeter, check there 
is no current flowing in the L8b
 relay circuits. Wires going to the rear terminals number 1, 2, 3,
 and 4 should have no current flowing in them.
 OR
 (ii) Carefully open the L8b relay cover and connect a regular 
digital or analog ammeter across one of the following Test Block Terminals 
(Across terminal 2 or across terminal 3, or across terminal 4.)
Using a small slot screwdriver, turn that same test block
 pin until it is in the horizontal "Test Position". 
There should
 be no current flow in the ammeter. Return the pin to its normal vertical
 (1) position and 
check the other terminals. 
 Note: Always check the continuity of the ammeter before using it
 in a (possible) live current circuit

Remove the relay DC isolating plug (located in the lower left comer of the 
relay)

Connect the two CT shorting links in the test block terminals as shown in 
Figure 2(b).

Use a small slot screwdriver to turn all test terminals to the horizontal 
(-) position.

Check all external connections to the relay and check terminal block wires 
are tight.

Inspect relay internally for any abnormalities: Loose connections, 
discolored or burned resistors, leaking capacitors, corrosion, unclean contacts 
(Clean with commercial Contact Cleaner. Burnish only if pitted.)

Using the relay settings supplied by EEC. and the manufacturer's 
information, check that all the appropriate settings have been correctly applied 
to the L8b relay.

Attach the multi-contact plug to the rear of the QZW415 Test Set and then 
connect the other end into the L8b relay test block
terminals

sections.text:
If this procedure is used for the L8a relay, short the 3-4 contact of the 
Pta 5 relay.

Keep the contact of the CM4 phase-to-phase relay open with a small piece of 
clean plastic when this unit is not being checked. This will avoid CM3 
calibration errors.

For the phase being tested, remove the blue coupling plug on the HG32 
Transformer and connect this plug to the QZW415 test terminal on the extreme 
left of group "e".

Referring to the calibration curves and the values calculated on the 3h test 
sheet (Pages no. 16, 17), determine the Z% value corresponding to the relay 
setting "A" of the first time-step.

Turn the %Z switches on the test set to agree with the calculated Zone 1 
setting.
Select single-phase-to-ground faults by turning switch "g" to position 2.

Select the phase fault by turning switch "f' to the positions R, S, T, 
respectively.
Insert the DC isolating plug into the relay

Push down and turn the voltage control switch n to
 the ON position (I).

Press button nl and observe when the CM3 Unit, the PTAW lockout contactor 
and the tripping contactor PD3 all pickup. (The red trip indication lamp on the 
test set will light when the tripping contactor operates).

Check for the next higher % Z setting at which the CM3, PFAW, and PD3 units 
do not operate, when the nl button is pressed.
Find the next lower setting at which the these units always pick up.
Repeat the above test about 5 times to determine the average pickup point.

Record the pickup point for this phase of the CM3
 relay on the 3h test sheet.
Repeat the above tests for all three phases (R, S, T).

Repeat the above test, Steps 4 to 15 above,
 once again, but this time, increase the % Z setting on the tester until
 the relay is operating in the second time-step. The CM3 and PD3 Units
 should operate and the lockout contactor PTAW should not operate.
For those relay schemes with an added third time step
 (zone) repeat Steps 4 to 15 above but increase the % Z
 setting on the tester to the third step operating level.

When checking the pickup value for 
the second time-step, the CUO under voltage contact of the "test" phase must be 
kept closed with a clean paper.
The mean value of all the above settings should agree with the curve 
(appendix-6r) or edeviate by a maximum of +/-5%.

When the CM3 pickup tests are 
completed, push down and turn the voltage control switch n to the OFF position 
(0).

Remove the DC isolating plug from the relay to
 de-energize the DC circuits.

All of these modem electronic timers only require start

sections.text:
The following Procedure Gives the Steps for using these Modem
Timers

Toggle switch "d" on the QZW415 to the
 sec position to select time measurements.

Use (2) test leads to connect the digital timer STOP
 inputs to terminal #12 and terminal # 13 (Yl) located in the top
 right comer of the QZW415 tester.
Press the reset button for the digital timer display.

items:
Toggle switch "d" on the QZW415 to the
 sec position to select time measurements.

Use (2) test leads to connect the digital 
 timer START inputs to the two QZW415 terminals #3 and #4 located in the bottom 
 right comer just above switch n.

Use (2) test leads to connect the digital timer STOP
 inputs to terminal #12 and terminal # 13 (Yl) located in the top
 right comer of the QZW415 tester.

Connect an AC supply to power the 
 electronic digital timer circuit.
Press the reset button for the digital timer display.

Repeat Steps from 1 to 15 as given earlier in this procedure to measure the Zone
 1, operation time
 for each of the CM3 units. Note: Set the line impedance % Z switches to a value which
 equals half the normal pickup value in the first time-step of the CM3
 unit. This will allow a good operation of the Zone I of the relay.
To perform the time test, press and hold switch nl in the closed position.
Measure and record the CM3 Zone I pickup time.

Increase the %Z setting on the QZW415 tester until the relay is operating in the 
second time step (as previously discussed in STEP 40) and measure the time. For 
those relay schemes with an added third time (zone) increase the %Z setting on 
the tester to the third step operating level and repeat timing tests to be as 
set out in the setting specifications for the third step. 
While testing the second (and third) time step, the
 contact of the CUO relay of the phase being tested should be kept closed.

When the CM3 pickup tests are completed, push down and
 turn the voltage control switch n to the OFF position (0).

Remove the D.C. isolating plug from the
 relay to de-energize the DC circuits.

Ensure That PT Circuit ON - Ensure That CT Circuit Closed - Ensure That DC is ON

items:
A continuously variable voltage source is required to
 properly test the CUO under voltage relays. When using switches h and k of
 the ABB QZW415 tester, voltages of up to 120 volts can be produced, but
 the variable voltages occur with interruptions due to using 
 switches.

This can result in inaccurate calibration of these units. Since a variable 
 rheostat is not available on the QZW415 tester, there are no procedures given 
 here. Future test equipment procedures detailing the testing of under voltage 
 relays can be used to perform these checks.
Ensure That PT Circuit ON - Ensure That CT Circuit Closed - Ensure That DC is ON

Referring to the calibration curves and the values calculated on the 3h test

Select single-phase-to-ground faults by turning switch "g" to position 2.

respectively.
Insert the DC isolating plug into the relay
Push down and turn the voltage control switch n to
 the ON position (I).
Press button nl and observe when the CM3 Unit, the PTAW lockout contactor 
and the tripping contactor PD3 all pickup. (The red trip indication lamp on the 
test set will light when the tripping contactor operates).
Check for the next higher % Z setting at which the CM3, PFAW, and PD3 units 
do not operate, when the nl button is pressed.
Find the next lower setting at which the these units always pick up.
Repeat the above test about 5 times to determine the average pickup point.
Record the pickup point for this phase of the CM3
 relay on the 3h test sheet.
Repeat the above tests for all three phases (R, S, T).
Repeat the above test, Steps 4 to 15 above,
 once again, but this time, increase the % Z setting on the tester until
 the relay is operating in the second time-step. The CM3 and PD3 Units
 should operate and the lockout contactor PTAW should not operate.
For those relay schemes with an added third time step
 (zone) repeat Steps 4 to 15 above but increase the % Z
 setting on the tester to the third step operating level.
When checking the pickup value for 
the second time-step, the CUO under voltage contact of the "test" phase must be 
kept closed with a clean paper.
The mean value of all the above settings should agree with the curve 
(appendix-6r) or edeviate by a maximum of +/-5%.
When the CM3 pickup tests are 
completed, push down and turn the voltage control switch n to the OFF position 
(0).

These older electromechanical motor/clock units have been
 superceded by more accurate digital timers such as the PROGRAMMER TM 14, or
 timers on the SVERKER 650 or the SIEMENS 7VP4800.
All of these modem electronic timers only require start
 and stop signals to accurately measure elapsed times.
The following Procedure Gives the Steps for using these Modem
Timers
Toggle switch "d" on the QZW415 to the
 sec position to select time measurements.
Use (2) test leads to connect the digital timer STOP
 inputs to terminal #12 and terminal # 13 (Yl) located in the top
 right comer of the QZW415 tester.
Press the reset button for the digital timer display.
Toggle switch "d" on the QZW415 to the
 sec position to select time measurements.
Use (2) test leads to connect the digital 
 timer START inputs to the two QZW415 terminals #3 and #4 located in the bottom 
 right comer just above switch n.
Use (2) test leads to connect the digital timer STOP
 inputs to terminal #12 and terminal # 13 (Yl) located in the top
 right comer of the QZW415 tester.
Connect an AC supply to power the 
 electronic digital timer circuit.
Press the reset button for the digital timer display.
Repeat Steps from 1 to 15 as given earlier in this procedure to measure the Zone
 1, operation time
 for each of the CM3 units. Note: Set the line impedance % Z switches to a value which
 equals half the normal pickup value in the first time-step of the CM3
 unit. This will allow a good operation of the Zone I of the relay.
To perform the time test, press and hold switch nl in the closed position.
Measure and record the CM3 Zone I pickup time.
Increase the %Z setting on the QZW415 tester until the relay is operating in the 
second time step (as previously discussed in STEP 40) and measure the time. For 
those relay schemes with an added third time (zone) increase the %Z setting on 
the tester to the third step operating level and repeat timing tests to be as 
set out in the setting specifications for the third step. 
While testing the second (and third) time step, the
 contact of the CUO relay of the phase being tested should be kept closed.
When the CM3 pickup tests are completed, push down and
 turn the voltage control switch n to the OFF position (0).
Remove the D.C. isolating plug from the
 relay to de-energize the DC circuits.
Repeat Steps from 1 to 15 as given earlier in this procedure to measure the Zone
 1, operation time
 for each of the CM3 units. Note: Set the line impedance % Z switches to a value which
 equals half the normal pickup value in the first time-step of the CM3
 unit. This will allow a good operation of the Zone I of the relay.
To perform the time test, press and hold switch nl in the closed position.
Press down and turn voltage control switch 
 n to the ON position (I). The timer will start and then stop once the PD3 trip 
 relay has picked up.
Measure and record the CM3 Zone I pickup time.
Repeat the test for the other two phases.
Increase the %Z setting on the QZW415 tester until the relay is operating in the 
second time step (as previously discussed in STEP 40) and measure the time. For 
those relay schemes with an added third time (zone) increase the %Z setting on 
the tester to the third step operating level and repeat timing tests to be as 
set out in the setting specifications for the third step. 
While testing the second (and third) time step, the
 contact of the CUO relay of the phase being tested should be kept closed.
When the CM3 pickup tests are completed, push down and
 turn the voltage control switch n to the OFF position (0).
Remove the D.C. isolating plug from the
 relay to de-energize the DC circuits.
Note: The Zone I tripping time should be about 25 milliseconds,
 but during the test it will be approximately 5 to 10 ms longer than the
 actual tripping time, because the relays are already energized before the
 fault occurs.

A continuously variable voltage source is required to
 properly test the CUO under voltage relays. When using switches h and k of
 the ABB QZW415 tester, voltages of up to 120 volts can be produced, but
 the variable voltages occur with interruptions due to using 
 switches.
This can result in inaccurate calibration of these units. Since a variable 
 rheostat is not available on the QZW415 tester, there are no procedures given 
 here. Future test equipment procedures detailing the testing of under voltage 
 relays can be used to perform these checks.
